title.narrative: Kathmandu Valley Water Supply Improvement Project

description.narrative: ADB and the Government of Nepal are working together to help the residents of the Kathmandu Valley to obtain greater access to clean water on a long-term basis. The Kathmandu Valley Water Supply Improvement Project is working to improve the efficiency and the reliability of the water supply system in the area while at the same time upgrading the infrastructure at the water source areas through a related project that is constructing the Melamchi tunnel and expanding the water treatment plant This project is expanding reservoirs, capacity and providing water connections with a focus on serving the poor and households headed by women. The long-term goal of the project is to provide affordable, clean water to the people of Kathmandu Valley for years to come.

title.narrative: Reports and Recommendations of the President

description.narrative: Improved access, efficiency, and reliability of water supply services to residents of Kathmandu Valley including poor women and men

Average pressure of supply at consumer-end increased from almost 0 meter in 2011 to at least 4 meter in all areas in 2016 Progress/Status: 24 hrs pilot distribution through new network (DMA-4.1 & 4.2) from Anamnagar OHT was managed. Recorded average pressure was about 1.0-1.5 bar. Average pressure in 17 tested DMAs has been recorded 2.5 kg/cm2 (2.53 bars). Data Source: Annual reports of KUKL, PID, MWS Actual value:

Compliance of water samples with national drinking water quality standards increased to more than 95% in 2016 Progress/Status: During supplied period, quality was measured in each SRT and quality was satisfying with national drinking water quality standards. Data Source: Annual reports of KUKL, PID, MWS Actual value:

Average supply improved from less than 1 hour every 4 days in 2011 to more than 2 hours daily in at least 80% of service area by 2016. At least 13 DMAs in service area (baseline 0) provided with 24x7 water supply. Achievement: 3 Progress/Status: Through new BDS, existing distribution network and tested new networks, water has again being supplied from Melamchi diversion from 9 October 2024 onwards after monsoon is over. Average supply in this period has remained consistent with about 3-4 hours in every three days time covering more than 80% service area. (July 2025) Data Source: Annual reports of KUKL, PID, MWS

Average availability of water improved from 45 lpcd in 2011 to 135 lpcd in at least 80% of service area in 2016 Progress/Status: Project has completed the testing and commissioning of all 32 DMAs and 981km pipe network, 84,000 house Service connection and 73,000 meters connection. SCADA is completed and in operation. Out of 32 DMA, 13 are handed over to KUKL, 11 are ready to be handed over to KUKL by August 2025 and rest will be handed over progressively. All capital works are completed. Loan closed for L2776 on Dec 2024 and for L3255 on June 2025. Average availability will be assessed during Project Completion Report preparation. ( July 2025) Data Source: Annual reports of KUKL, PID, MWS Actual value:
Output/s as listed by the project staff.
Output: Operating and financial systems improved, and capacities strengthened Indicator: 30% are women. Achievement: 30 Data Source: Project progress reports prepared by KUKL, KVWSMB, and MWS

Output: Operating and financial systems improved, and capacities strengthened Indicator: At least 20% of citizens participate in public meetings in DNI areas, as per GESI action plan Achievement: 30 Progress/Status: Community awareness and safeguards consultants were mobilized to support PID for implementation of gender equality and social inclusion (GESI) action plan, resettlement plan and grievance redress system, and various other community awareness campaigns and ensuring contractors compliance to safeguards requirements.
2,415 consultations/meetings have been conducted in the communities so far. Out of the total of 109,814 individuals' participants, 58,767 (53.562%) were men and 51,067(46.38%) were women. Data Source: Project progress reports prepared by KUKL, KVWSMB, and MWS

Output: Operating and financial systems improved, and capacities strengthened Indicator: Public education activities conducted in at least 50 schools per year as per GESI action plan Achievement: 664 Progress/Status: Public Education and School Health Programs have been conducted in 684 schools so far. Out of the total of 32,877 participants, 16,109 (49%) were girls and 16,768 (51%) were boys. (July 2024) Data Source: Project progress reports prepared by KUKL, KVWSMB, and MWS
